title: Incident Response: Communications, RBAC & Evidence Preservation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook standardizes how Redwood responds to security incidents that require coordinated communications, RBAC control changes, and legally defensible evidence preservation. It combines technical runbook steps, communications templates, and an evidence packaging workflow to ensure traceability for audits and regulators.

Intended audience:
Security responders, SREs, incident commanders, platform engineers, legal, and product owners.

Scope and exclusions:
- Applies to incidents that trigger data access investigations, suspected exfiltration, privilege escalation, or audit log tampering.
- Excludes routine operational alerts that do not indicate unauthorized access (see monitoring playbook).

Goals and success criteria:
- Preserve a verifiable, tamper-evident evidence set within 4 hours of incident declaration.
- Implement emergency RBAC changes within 30 minutes of classification when needed.
- Notify internal stakeholders and legal within SLA: 60 minutes for high-severity incidents.

Owners and roles

- Incident Commander (IC): directs response, approves communications. (Security on-call)
- Evidence Custodian: owns evidence capture and packaging. (Security forensics)
- RBAC Owner: performs role/permission adjustments and documents changes. (IAM team)
- SRE Lead: performs containment actions on infra and app tiers.
- Legal / Privacy: assesses legal hold and regulator notification requirements.
- Comms Lead: drafts internal and external messaging.

Pre-incident configuration checklist

1) RBAC mapping inventory (maintain as a living table in the IAM repo):
| Role | Scope | Owner | Emergency revocation contact |
|---|---|---|---|
| svc-platform-admin | Cluster-wide, production | IAM Team | iam-oncall@redwood.ai |
| redwood-security-ops | Incident response privileges | Security | sec-oncall@redwood.ai |
| analytics-readonly | Data lake read-only | Data Platform | data-platform@redwood.ai |

2) Audit logging baseline configuration (minimum):
- All API gateway requests: request_id, user_id, client_ip, headers subset, timestamp, route, response_code.
- Auth events (success/failure): user, method, source, timestamp, reason.
- Privileged actions: role changes, token creations/revocations, service-account key rotations.

3) Retention and integrity controls:
- Short-term hot logs: 90 days (fast-query SLA).
- Long-term archive: 7 years (WORM-backed storage where required).
- Log immutability: Writes to the archive are S3 Object Lock enabled; HMAC checksums recorded in the evidence index.

Incident classification matrix

Severity | Trigger examples | Immediate RBAC action
---|---|---
P1 / Critical | Confirmed data exfiltration or active lateral movement | Revoke affected service-account keys + block user sessions
P2 / High | Suspected privilege escalation or abnormal admin activity | Scoped role removal, require reauth via MFA
P3 / Medium | Unusual access but no signs of compromise | Increased monitoring, session token refresh

Detection & triage (first 60 minutes)

1) Declare incident and assign roles. IC posts incident page and sets severity.
2) Triage checklist (run in parallel):
- Evidence Custodian: snapshot current audit streams and store in evidence bucket with immutable flag. CLI example:
  - aws s3 cp s3://audit-stream/current/ s3://evidence-bucket/INC-<id>/raw/ --recursive --storage-class STANDARD_IA --metadata status=sealed
  - Record object checksums: sha256sum *.log > manifest.sha256
- RBAC Owner: list recent privileged changes: run:
  - gcloud logging read "resource.type=project AND protoPayload.methodName:('SetIamPolicy' OR 'CreateServiceAccountKey')" --limit 500 --format json > recent-privileged.json
- SRE Lead: isolate suspected hosts/subnets (apply network ACLs or kill sessions).
- IC: notify Legal and Comms.

Evidence preservation step-by-step (technical)

1. Snapshot live logs and metadata:
- Capture current offsets/checkpoints for streaming systems (Kafka):
  - kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server broker:9092 --describe --group audit-consumer > kafka-checkpoints.txt
- Snapshot cloud metadata: instance list, IAM policy versions, active sessions.

2. Create an evidence container (one per incident):
- Naming convention: INC-<YYYYMMDD>-<short-id> (e.g., INC-20270208-7c4f)
- Location: s3://evidence-bucket/INC-20270208-7c4f/ with Object Lock enabled and retention date set to policy (7 years when required).

3. Compute and record cryptographic integrity proofs:
- For every file added, produce sha256 and store in manifest.sha256. Example manifest entry:
  - 3f786850e387550fdab836ed7e6dc881de23001b  2027-02-08T14:12:00Z  logs/gateway-2027-02-08T14:00.log
- Sign the manifest using the Evidence Custodian's GPG key and store signature as manifest.sha256.sig.

4. Freeze relevant access controls:
- Create a temporary deny policy applied to affected roles/users. Example (pseudo-YAML):
  - deny: true
    principals: [user:alice@redwood.ai, svc:batch-processor]
    resources: [projects/redwood-prod/*]
    expires_at: 2027-02-15T00:00:00Z
- Document the change in the incident timeline (automatically via the incident system).

Communications & escalation workflow

Internal notifications (timeline SLA):
- 0-60 minutes: Notify Security, SRE, Legal, Product, and Exec (severity P1 only). Use secured channel: #inc-<id>-priv (Slack private) and send email to incident-distribution@redwood.ai.
- 60-180 minutes: Prepare public-facing statement draft if data exposure confirmed.

Templates (examples)
- Internal Slack opener (private channel):
  - "INC-<id> declared (P1). IC: @<name>. Do not share outside this channel. Evidence snapshot in s3://evidence-bucket/INC-<id>/. Legal on call: @legal-oncall."
- Executive email summary (first 180 minutes):
  - Subject: INC-<id> — High severity incident — initial summary
  - Body: concise incident time, systems impacted, containment stage, next steps, and expected update cadence.

Outside communications and regulator notifications

- Legal must approve any external notification. Use the external comms checklist: confirm facts, authorized spokesperson, data categories affected, remediation steps, and regulator reporting deadlines (per jurisdiction).

Compliance evidence workflow (audit-ready packaging)

1) Evidence index entry (example fields recorded in the evidence registry):
- incident_id, artifact_path, sha256, captured_by, capture_time, access_control_snapshot_path, retention_policy_id, signature_path.
2) Export for auditor: prepare a read-only bundle with manifest and signature and provide time-limited access URL and audit trail of access.
3) Change log: every RBAC change performed as part of incident must be recorded with pre/post policy diffs and stored in the incident timeline.

Post-incident actions (72 hours to 30 days)

1) 72-hour initial report: IC and Evidence Custodian produce a technical summary and list of mitigations.
2) 7-day remediation plan: fix root cause, rotate credentials, and implement permanent RBAC changes if needed.
3) 30-day review: run an evidence integrity audit and tabletop to exercise lessons learned.

Exceptions and risk acceptance

- If immediate evidence preservation conflicts with live containment (e.g., capturing live memory will crash a service), the IC must document the decision, alternative preservation steps, and obtain Legal sign-off.
- Any temporary RBAC deny that lasts longer than 7 days requires approval from IAM manager and Security Director.

Operational runbook snippets (quick commands)

- Collect active SSH sessions (Linux):
  - sudo lsof -iTCP -sTCP:ESTABLISHED -nP | grep ssh > /tmp/ssh-sessions.txt
- Export IAM policy diff (AWS example):
  - aws iam get-role --role-name redwood-admin --output json > role-before.json
  - # make change
  - aws iam get-role --role-name redwood-admin --output json > role-after.json
  - diff -u role-before.json role-after.json > role-policy-diff.patch

Evidence retention mapping (summary table)

| Artifact type | Hot retention | Archive retention | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| API gateway logs | 90 days | 7 years | Platform Observability Team |
| Auth events | 365 days | 7 years | IAM Team |
| Privileged action logs | 365 days | 7 years | Security Forensics |

Appendices

A. Investigator checklist (short)
- Verify incident declaration and ID
- Establish private coordination channel
- Snapshot logs and verify checksums
- Freeze or snapshot RBAC policies
- Notify Legal and Comms

B. Evidence naming and retention policy (reference):
- Naming: INC-YYYYMMDD-<id>/<artifact-type>/<filename>
- Retention labels: incident:short (90d), incident:standard (1y), incident:regulatory (7y)
